items.title: Capture each raid's snapshot at its own start, from a log of sign-up and placement changes
items.notes: GitHub issue #149: stewartalex4-art handed it to jeffkyle91 on 2026-10-30, claimed on #149; priority raised to high by the loot owner on 2026-10-31. Goal: capture each raid's starting snapshot at its own start instead of the 9:00 PM ET daily run, so a later raid has it the same night and live display fields are read at the start. First step (loot owner, 2026-11-08; replaces the log-first plan posted on #149): the existing sweep runs every five minutes (UTC, 240-second timeout, no scheduler retries) and works as of two minutes before each scheduled run; a transient failure retries after 5 minutes, doubling to at most 6 hours; a sign-up or working roster saved up to a minute after the start counts, because every writer refuses changes once it has passed, and the allowance ends sooner if the raid was edited after its start; a raid created just before its start counts too, and overlapping runs leave each other's capture alone. No new Google service, index, rules or UI; an idle run costs about six reads and one write, about 1,700 reads a day. Functions tests in functions/raidStartSnapshot.test.js. First step deployed in 2026-11-08 - 6721a31. Remaining, open for the maintainer on #149: a task per raid (Cloud Tasks as a dependency), the append-only log of sign-up and placement changes (who reads it, how long it is kept, a first event for earlier sign-ups), and retrying a terminal failure (RAID-015's notice).

items.title: Show started and failed raid snapshots in Raid History
items.notes: GitHub issue #150; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. Built on feat/raid-snapshot-status, PR #178. Rules: active members read a starting snapshot's manifest while capturing, complete or failed, and its lineup, character and account records whenever the manifest is; a list must ask for those statuses; strangers, other guilds and removed members read nothing, and there are no client writes (rules tests for each status and role). Capture: a terminal failure before any manifest exists also writes a small visible failed record at snapshots/start (failureNotice: the raid's name and date at the start, the scheduled start, the failure code and time, never the server detail); the server-only failure record, the log line and a capturing manifest becoming failed are unchanged (Functions tests). Raid History > Audit Info: queries those three statuses, a Complete, In progress or Failed chip on each entry, a banner while capturing ("this list may be incomplete", n of m records written) or failed (plain words for every failure code, the code in small text); a lineup not written is its own entry, never an empty team. Checked with a local seed read back as a Member through the rules, and in a browser as Member, Raid Leader, Guild Leader and VIEW AS, light and dark, at 320px. Out of scope: a retry (RAID-014), paging and per-raid summaries (after RAID-019), an alert to leaders (OPS-001). Failures recorded before deployment have no visible record. Deployed with Firestore rules before Hosting in bb1a2d2.

items.title: Show a Signups board and the Groups workbench as tabs in an opened scheduled raid
items.notes: GitHub issue #167; approved by the maintainer on the issue ("Approved as proposed"). Requested by the guild's loot owner. Implemented in PR #175 on feat/raid-signups-board. An opened Scheduled Raids row has two tabs (the ARIA tabs pattern, 44px): Signups, a read-only board like Discord's Raid Helper (Accept responses in Tanks, Healers, Ranged and Melee columns split by class with counts, class colors and spec icons, then Bench, Tentative, Late, Absent and Not responded, the invited members with no response), and Groups, the workbench unchanged (ScheduledRaidWorkbench.tsx and ScheduledRaidRoster.tsx untouched). Members open on Signups, Guild and Raid Leaders on Groups. Both tabs read the row's one sign-up and planning subscription, so switching tabs subscribes nothing. Pure grouping in features/scheduled-raids/signupGroups.ts, unit tested for 10, 20 and 40 players and a raid with no responses. No rules, data or Functions change. Out of scope: sign-up order numbers and the leader-only View activity log button (both need RAID-014's log), Discord sign-ups (DISCORD-001), attendance (RAID-005). Browser checks (leader and member, light and dark, 375px and 320px, listener counts) are documented in PR #175.

items.title: List every raid with its category in Raid History and let leaders mark a raid complete
items.notes: GitHub issue #168; approved by the maintainer on the issue ("Approved as proposed"). Requested by the loot owner. Every raid has one category: Scheduled, In Progress, Complete (a Guild or Raid Leader pressed Mark complete, or 5 hours have passed since its start, whichever comes first) or Cancelled (at any time). Built on feat/raid-categories, PR #177. Scheduled Raids and Raid History share the raid category rule. firestore.rules accept raid status 'complete' only from Guild and Raid Leaders, after the saved start, never straight from cancelled, with an audit entry whose action is 'complete'; undo is an audited edit back to scheduled. Scheduled Raids chips say In Progress, Complete or Cancelled, and an opened row of a raid in progress has Mark complete (Undo complete once marked) for leaders. Raid History opens on All raids: every raid newest first from data already loaded (no new Firestore read), with category, month and phase filters and Show more; Audit Info is unchanged. Automatic snapshots still capture completed raids. Phase filter (loot owner, 2026-10-29: give each loot phase a start date): settings keep phaseStarts, one Eastern date per finished and current phase; starting a phase records today, reopening removes it, and a Guild Leader sets or corrects dates in Settings > Loot phases, each an audited phase entry ('edit'); the rules refuse dates that go backwards. A raid is in the latest phase that started on or before its date. Partial delivery (categories, Mark complete, and phase filtering) deployed in bb1a2d2. Remaining: the failed-capture warning in All raids and a count of reads on opening Raid History. Coordinate with RAID-015 (#150), RAID-014 (#149) and proposed RAID-020, which also changes raid status values.

items.title: Show scheduled raids as collapsible banners with zone artwork
items.notes: GitHub issue #146; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. Scheduled Raids becomes a list of collapsed rows with no dropdown: each has a banner of its raid's zone pictures (every zone, side by side, each fading into the next; a color tint for a zone without a picture) and the raid's name, date, time and status. Opening a row shows today's roster, sign-ups and buff coverage and starts that raid's listeners only. Add Raid and Edit Raid show the zone pictures. A new shared banner in src/shared/raids/. On the first-raid path (Dec 9): land after RAID-013 and leave the roster workbench untouched. No rules or data change. Built on feat/scheduled-raid-banners: a shared RaidBanner and raidZoneArt (a raid zone's picture is found from its stored id; the small copy is used and loaded lazily), rows in features/scheduled-raids/ (RaidRow, groupRaids), and Add Raid and Edit Raid show each zone's picture and a banner preview. A row mounts its panel only while open, so closed rows start no listener. A raid is listed from the moment it is scheduled until 5 hours after its start, then leaves the list (Raid History keeps it); this replaces the issue's collapsed group of past raids, per the loot owner on 2026-10-27. Deployed in 0d9ed00.

items.title: Show zone pictures on the upcoming raids of My dashboard
items.notes: GitHub issue #154; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. Each upcoming raid on My dashboard shows its zones' pictures, using the shared banner of RAID-016 (no new reads). Follows RAID-016 and MEMBER-006. Built on feat/dashboard-raid-art: each upcoming raid row gets a 40px strip of its zones' pictures (the shared RaidBanner; a zone with no picture shows its color tint), placed first by CSS with the strip as the row's last child so no existing child moves; the text and the sign-up button stay on the plain surface. Feature-local (src/features/dashboard): no data, rules or read change. Checked in the local emulators as a Member: rows with no zones and with 1, 2, 3 and 10 zones, the unavailable state, the sign-up dialog, View on calendar, light and dark, 375px and 320px. Not checked: a screen reader, Firefox, Safari. Deployed in 0d9ed00.

items.title: Complete audited loot write helpers and enforcement

items.notes: PR #144 deployed via Hosting in fa95142 on October 24; receipts on #140/#143/#144. Spreadsheet/addon import remains LOOT-005; spreadsheet receipts remain a fallback. Included in this cumulative release record.

items.notes: GitHub issue #12 (A3), resolved by the released roster-picker workflow. Deployed through edb344a and included in this verified cumulative release. Roster-picked candidates and award recipients carry stable character IDs; completion, filters and My dashboard follow recorded IDs through renames. Award candidate-order and council-note snapshots remain immutable, and historical award/Log names are retained. Legacy priorities convert on leader edit; unmatched names remain notes. Older name-only awards are not retroactively rewritten. Standalone no-priority awards remain LOOT-002.

items.title: Add award correction and removal UI and readable audit history
items.notes: Issue #11 (A2); remaining correction/removal UI in #140 deployed via Hosting as fa95142 on October 24, included in this cumulative record. Guild/Raid Leaders unlock a priority and use x beside RECEIVED to move a receipt or remove it with a reason. Each change is an audited batch; no hard deletion or snapshot edits. Removed awards stop counting in completion, dashboard and header; legacy awards retain their original Log row. Build/lint, 769 unit and 233 targeted award-rules tests passed, including correction/removal of the manual form's payload. Both production domains matched built assets; no production award mutations. Receipt on #140. Earlier permanent Log shipped in 92dbc71. Issue closure remains the maintainer's decision; no issue is closed by this documentation update.

items.title: Import spreadsheet and addon awards with validated preview
items.notes: GitHub issue #21 (B6) spans this import scope and standalone manual entry in LOOT-002; neither is completed by awards through priority notes. Agree formats, duplicate detection and recipient matching. Preserve original award dates separately from later entry/audit timestamps. Support recovery of December 9 spreadsheet receipts. Preview must mark errors/duplicates and require confirmation; every import is audited and manual entry must work without external lookup. Formats and safety rules agreed in GitHub issue #165 (maintainer, 2026-10-27); the design is docs/design/award-import.md on docs/award-import, PR #181. Spreadsheet columns approved by the loot owner on 2026-10-30; the maintainer's approval is pending. The importer is not built. Conflicts (loot owner, 2026-11-12, #193): a row that differs from an award already imported is a Conflict the uploader resolves per award (keep the app's, use the import's, or pick per field) or all at once; addon awards store sourceRev, so an older copy shows as Stale.

items.title: Complete main/alt priority policy and alt-only-run controls
items.notes: Not being built for now (2026-10-27): the loot owner decided the mains-over-alts rule is guild policy, not something the site needs to enforce. PR #163 and issue #162 are closed; the branch feat/mains-first-warning stays on the fork. Reopen if the guild wants the warning. Earlier notes, for reference: Priority adoption is expected around December 15. Confirm wording and per-raid exception; priorities are not required for initial loot recording. Decided by the loot owner (2026-10-24): mains get loot priority over alts, shown as a warning only (a leader sees, for example, that two mains still need the item and decides), not enforced; the alt-only exception is a tick in the Award loot and Record loot dialogs that silences the warning for that award (client only; the reason goes in the award note), for runs of any size; wording "Mains get loot prio over alts".

items.title: Add item/loot-table data and remaining priority filters

Settings Zones supplies dungeon and raid catalog entries to scheduling and drop lists. Class/Needs players toolbar filters were replaced; Needs players remains a row marker. Remaining: only-items-with-a-priority filter and confirmation of complete Forever loot data. Nine bundled dungeons remain beta practice data, not game-verified facts.

Through d0ef75d: Guild/Raid Leaders paste item IDs or Wowhead links with name previews, add/reorder creatures and add/remove/restore items; phase zone checklists use the Settings Zones catalog. items.title: Add items from Browse drops to the priority list and assign players

items.title: Show the loot phase on every Log entry and filter the Log by phase and by raid night
items.notes: Existing mapping from issue #141 retained without changing priority/target. PR #143 deployed via Hosting in fa95142 on October 24; receipt on #143. Phase column, phase search/filter and raid-date filter delivered. Awards use awardedAt; other entries use their entry day. Unknown phase shows a dash. Build/lint and 769 unit tests passed for the combined release; production assets matched on both domains. Filters apply to loaded entries (newest 100 first; Load older entries goes further back). An award stores no raid link: Date plus dungeon/boss distinguishes different dungeons, not two runs of the same dungeon or missing dungeon data. A stored raid link remains deferred until needed; if built, 20- and 10-player raids are separate pre-scheduled events, larger first, with audited leader reassignment. Client only; included in this cumulative release record. Mapping confirmed by the maintainer in the linked issue, as recorded in #158.

items.title: List recently recorded awards so leaders can move or remove any of them
items.notes: GitHub issue #170. ID proposed in #170, awaiting the maintainer's confirmation (it is not LOOT-008, which is editing the drop lists); the priority and target here are proposed with it, since every December 9 award is a Record loot award. Built (the PR number follows): a Recent awards button beside Record loot, shown on the same terms (a leader looking at the current phase; hidden in the VIEW AS preview), opens Recently recorded: every award of the current phase, with or without a priority list, newest raid night first and then the latest entered, 30 at a time with Show 30 more. A removed award is struck through, with its reason and no Fix. Fix opens the existing receipt-fix dialog, whose priority is now optional (a Record loot award gets the roster alone), so the move, the removal, the reason rules, the stale-award check and the audited batch are unchanged. No rules or shared-file change: the existing manual-award rules tests cover the move and removal payloads. Unit tests pin the order, phase filter, paging and row state. Production assets were verified after deployment. Emulator checks used VIEW AS; actual Raid Leader and Member sign-ins, unlocked-priority x behavior, and stale-award behavior in a second tab were not exercised. Out of scope: fixing awards of a finished phase, restoring a removed award, undoing an import in bulk (LOOT-005), returning to the list after a fix. Open in #170: which phase the December 9 awards fall in (#142, OPS-005).

items.title: Add Removed member status and no-access screen
items.notes: GitHub issue #14 (A5), resolved by #75. Deployed in a36ba48 and verified; included in this cumulative release summary. Guild Leader-only removal/restoration with confirmation, no self-removal, atomic unlinking, backend access denial and live no-access screen. Characters, assignments, history and Auth account remain. Restoration grants unlinked Member access, requiring explicit relinking/promotion.

items.title: Add character-change requests and leader approvals

items.title: Erase the pre-launch test data once, at launch, with a maintainer-run script
items.notes: GitHub issue #142, PR #159: the maintainer agreed to a one-time maintainer-run script, its scope (that phase's awards, loot priorities and the Log entries about them) and the AGENTS.md exception; the maintainer confirms the ID, priority and target. The maintainer preferred Jeff to run it while the maintainer monitors and supports (#142); coordinate the date, confirm the dry-run numbers and take a full Firestore export first. Requested by the guild's loot owner: everything recorded in Launch prep was beta and testing and should not count, appear on dashboards or sit in the permanent record once the first real phase starts; the Log is immutable from then on. The rules (and AGENTS.md) never allow an award or Log entry to be deleted, so this is a script the maintainer runs once with the Admin SDK, not an app feature: dry run by default, confirmed counts and project, a typed phrase, a backup file read back before any delete, a guard that only the finished phase is erased, a check that nothing is left, then a seal and a visible Log record, and a refusal to run twice. Erases that phase's awards, loot priorities and the Log entries about them; keeps everything else. Tested with invented data in the emulator and in a separate real Firestore test project; production was not touched. The test-project rehearsal did not cover interruption/resume or the Log display. See docs/design/launch-reset.md. Merged in #159; Log display support was deployed in ee20765 (receipt on #159). Maintainer rehearsal/adoption and the one-time production reset have not been performed; do not mark the reset released from a merge or Hosting deploy.
